question: What is the main goal of injection safety protocols in nursing?

options.A: Speeding up medication administration during busy shifts
options.B: Eliminating the need for personal protective equipment
options.C: Ensuring procedures cause no harm to recipients or providers
options.D: Reducing the overall cost of hospital consumables

explanation: Spot on! Injection safety is all about protecting everyone involved—patients, nurses, and the community—by following clean, safe handling habits. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T2#GNS122_U3_T2_h1)

question: When a clinic is short on supplies and staff are overworked, what dangerous practice often happens?

options.A: Taking shortcuts with sterile injection protocols
options.C: Prolonging the recovery time of surgical patients
options.D: Increasing the frequency of patient vital sign checks

explanation: You've got this. When the pressure is high and supplies are low, nurses can feel rushed, which sadly leads to cutting corners on infection control. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T2#GNS122_U3_T2_h1)

question: What is the biggest danger of reusing a single syringe for more than one patient?

options.A: Guaranteed development of sterile skin abscesses
options.B: Direct transfer of bloodborne pathogens between individuals
options.C: Rapid expiration of the remaining vial contents
options.D: Immediate crystallization of the administered medication

explanation: Never reuse needles or syringes! Doing this easily moves microscopic blood and germs from one patient right into the next. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T2#GNS122_U3_T2_h2)

question: Why is it unsafe to push a needle you've already used back into a multi-dose medication vial?

options.A: It increases the physical pressure inside the glass container
options.B: It instantly neutralizes the active chemical ingredients
options.C: It contaminates the entire vial with pathogens
options.D: It causes the rubber stopper to dissolve completely

explanation: A used needle carries germs straight into the clean medicine, turning the whole vial into a hazard for anyone else who needs it. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T2#GNS122_U3_T2_h2)

question: Which blood-borne virus spread by unsafe injections currently does NOT have a vaccine?
explanation: Great to know for clinical practice: while we have a vaccine for Hepatitis B, Hepatitis C doesn't have one yet, making strict sterile technique our best shield! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T2#GNS122_U3_T2_h3)

question: Why do contaminated needles and syringes spread infections so easily?

options.A: Patients have lowered systemic immunity during hospital admissions
options.B: Viruses multiply rapidly when exposed to standard room lighting
options.C: Equipment directly breaches the skin barrier into vascular or tissue spaces
options.D: Medications react chemically with viral particles to enhance potency

explanation: Remember, the skin is our first line of defense. An injection bypasses that barrier, giving germs on a dirty needle a direct doorway into the body. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T2#GNS122_U3_T2_h3)

question: What can happen if an intramuscular injection is given incorrectly in the buttocks and strikes the sciatic nerve?

options.C: Permanent nerve damage or foot drop

explanation: This is why proper landmarking (like the ventrogluteal site or upper outer quadrant) is so crucial! Hitting the sciatic nerve causes intense pain and can lead to foot drop. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T2#GNS122_U3_T2_h4)

question: A patient develops a painful, swollen lump filled with pus a few days after an injection. What is this called?
explanation: Spot on. When bacteria get introduced during an injection, they can cause a localized collection of pus known as an abscess. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T2#GNS122_U3_T2_h4)

question: Which common habit among nurses is a leading cause of accidental needle stick injuries?

options.C: Using multi-dose vials for multiple patients

explanation: Never recap with two hands! Trying to slide a needle back into its cap puts your fingers right in the path of a accidental poke. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T2#GNS122_U3_T2_h5)

question: Why is experiencing a needle stick injury so emotionally stressful for a healthcare worker?

options.A: Hospital management automatically terminates staff who experience punctures
options.B: Occupational health laws forbid workers from taking sick leave
options.C: Treatment for accidental punctures requires immediate major surgery
options.D: Workers face anxiety and stigma from potential blood-borne infections

explanation: It's completely normal to feel anxious; the worry of catching something like HIV or Hepatitis from a quick poke weighs heavily on healthcare staff. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T2#GNS122_U3_T2_h5)

question: Where should the sharps container be placed when you are about to give an injection?

options.A: Near the nurses' station desk for charting
options.B: Directly outside the main ward entrance
options.C: Inside the clean utility storage room
options.D: Immediately adjacent to the point of use

explanation: Always keep your sharps box right beside you during the procedure so you can drop the needle in immediately without walking across the room. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T2#GNS122_U3_T2_h6)

question: How do safety-engineered injection devices help protect nurses?

options.A: By incorporating physical mechanisms that shield or retract the needle
options.B: By eliminating the need for any hand hygiene before procedures
options.C: By chemically dissolving the needle immediately after medication delivery
options.D: By changing color when the needle is contaminated with bacteria

explanation: These clever tools have built-in guards or spring-backs that cover the sharp tip automatically once you finish your injection. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T2#GNS122_U3_T2_h6)

question: What common belief in many communities leads patients to demand injections instead of oral drugs?

options.A: Assuming that injections prevent all forms of chronic illness
options.B: Believing that needles are completely painless when administered correctly
options.C: Thinking that oral medications are more expensive than injections
options.D: Believing that injectable medications work faster or better than oral drugs

explanation: Many patients feel a jab is more powerful than a tablet, which is a big reason why community education on safe medication use is so important! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T2#GNS122_U3_T2_h7)

question: You see a fellow student nurse trying to recap a used needle. What is the best thing to do?

options.A: Stop the colleague and demonstrate safe sharps disposal into a nearby bin
options.B: Wait until the shift ends to report the unsafe habit to the hospital board
options.C: Take over all injection duties for the remainder of the clinical shift
options.D: Ignore the action since no patient has been injured yet

explanation: We look out for each other! Kindly stopping unsafe habits right away helps keep your entire clinical team safe from injuries. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T2#GNS122_U3_T2_h7)
